biomechanical_root_cause: Hips shooting up prematurely before the barbell passes the knees. Caused by either starting with the hips positioned too low (squatting the deadlift), weak quadriceps unable to initiate the knee extension push off the floor, or the bar starting too far forward of midfoot.
verbal_cues: Leg press the floor away from you on the initial pull.
Chest and hips must rise at the exact same angle until the bar clears the knees.
Keep the weight centered over the middle of your foot.

corrective_drills.coaching_points: Break the bar off the floor, pause 2 seconds 1 inch up while holding torso angle constant, then drive through to lockout. Builds position-specific quad endurance.
Increases knee flexion at setup, forcing stronger leg drive off the floor.

biomechanical_root_cause: Dropping hips below knee level before pulling, pushing the shins forward and knocking the barbell away from the midfoot center of gravity.
verbal_cues: Deadlift is a hinge, not a squat. Set hips high between knees and shoulders.
Bring shins to the bar without dropping your hips lower.

corrective_drills.coaching_points: Teaches the pure hip-hinge pattern while keeping knees soft and hips high.

biomechanical_root_cause: Leaning the upper torso backward at the top of the deadlift rather than driving the hips forward into terminal extension. Places high compressive and shear stress on the lumbar facet joints and discs.
verbal_cues: Stand straight up like a soldier; do not lean back.
Squeeze your glutes to finish the pull, not your lower back.

corrective_drills.coaching_points: Locks the pelvis in neutral and isolates glute extension without permitting spinal arching.

biomechanical_root_cause: Failure to engage the latissimus dorsi to pull the bar into the body, increasing the moment arm between the barbell and the lumbar spine.
verbal_cues: Protect your armpits: imagine holding an orange under each armpit and squeezing the juice out.
Paint your shins and thighs with the barbell.

corrective_drills.coaching_points: Anchor a light resistance band to a rack in front of the bar. Forces active lat engagement to keep the bar against the legs.
